"fab40d01-6a17-5e12-835f-851b2c004a35" :question/problem "Express the following as a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
6\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right)\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{9}\right)
$$"] [:db/add "fab40d01-6a17-5e12-835f-851b2c004a35" :question/worked-solution "Put $x=\frac{2\pi}{9}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
6\sin x\cos x &=3\left[2\sin x\cos x\right] \\ &=3\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=\frac{2\pi}{9}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. The result is

$$
3\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right) .
$$"] [:db/add "fab40d01-6a17-5e12-835f-851b2c004a35" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "fab40d01-6a17-5e12-835f-851b2c004a35" :question/answer-fields "8854730c-c3da-5f60-9589-440fbe88c48c" :question/problem "Simplify.

\end{aligned}

"93b7d1d0-7e49-52ca-9461-bf09a9381e7c" :question/problem "Simplify.

$$
\left(\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right)+\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{9}\right)\right)^2
$$"] [:db/add "93b7d1d0-7e49-52ca-9461-bf09a9381e7c" :question/worked-solution "Put $x=\frac{4\pi}{9}$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x+\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1+2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1+\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
